title: Interpret a quadratic graph in context

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: The height h metres of a ball t seconds after it is thrown is modelled by h = -t^2 + 6t + 7. Find the maximum height of the ball and the time when this happens.
student_prompt: Use completed-square form or another clear method.
expected_answer: Maximum height 16 m at t = 3 s

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: Because the coefficient of t^2 is negative, the turning point is a maximum, not a minimum.
Factor out the negative first: h = -(t^2 - 6t) + 7, so the square involves (t - 3)^2.

hint_ladder.title: What does the context ask for?
hint_ladder.prompt: Maximum height corresponds to the turning point of a downward-opening quadratic. Think about the graph shape before calculating.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Because the squared term has a negative coefficient, factor that negative before completing the square.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students complete the square as if the leading coefficient were positive, or identify the turning point but do not translate it into time and height.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For h = -t^2 + bt + c, complete the square by handling the negative leading term, then interpret the turning point as time and height. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

expected_solution_steps.action: factor out negative and complete the square
common_errors: does not factor out the negative
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is completing the square when the t^2 coefficient is negative.
The stuck point is reading the turning point from completed-square form.
The stuck point is interpreting the turning point in the context of the ball's height.

mark_scheme_notes: Award marks for completed-square form or equivalent turning point method, maximum height, time, and units.
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: mishandling the negative leading coefficient and not interpreting the turning point in context.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, how does the negative coefficient affect the graph shape?
